sections.title: Property Sheet — P-HOUSE
sections.md:
| # | Field | Value |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Type and era | **(v2 — your Fix "change the house")** 1960s red-brick ex-council end-of-terrace in a Kent town; a builder's house kept well by people who never redecorated — solid, warm, a little dated; the same couple thirty years |
| 2 | Shell | pale sage-green emulsion over woodchip · low square dark-oak skirting · dark-oak architraves · 1960s teak-veneer flush doors, round brass knobs · white Artex swirl ceilings · deep burgundy carpet through hall, stairs, landing and bedrooms → brown-and-orange patterned lino at the kitchen threshold · cream steel panel radiators · brown-edged cream switches |
| 3 | Floor map | front door → a roomy hall; the stairs rise straight up the LEFT-hand wall, 13 steep burgundy steps, dark handrail and turned spindles on the open right side, square dark newel post, a cupboard under the stairs; front room off the hall on the right; the kitchen at the far end, its back door onto the garden; the back bedroom off the landing |
| 4 | Orientation | front door and street face east (morning sun down the street); the back (kitchen, back bedroom, garden) faces west — the low evening sun over the garden wall |
| 5 | Carried elements | the dark handrail, turned spindles and square newel post · the long mirror, key shelf and coat rack on the right-hand wall (his navy work jacket, her camel coat, a hi-vis vest) · his tan work boots on the mat · the brass three-arm light |
| 6 | Exterior | the red-brick terrace street with low front walls and cars along both kerbs; the long narrow back garden with brick wall and fence, lawn, raised beds, shed — the near half becoming the sandstone patio |
| 7 | Standing negatives | none observed yet |

**Plates:** 10 Sunburst renders, 16:9, 2688×1520, 2.75 cr each (27.50; Higgsfield → about 5,825). Prompts `plates/<ID>.prompt.txt` from `plates/build_plates.py` (`CAM-FILM` wide on a tripod → `PLATE-PROP` / `PROP-REF` + `PROP-SHELL` + the room → `VIEW-OUT` → `PROD-DEPTH` → `LIGHT-FILM` → `LOOK-HERDAD` → `PHYS-FRAME-C` → `CAP-FILM` → negatives). The three house rooms were made with P-HOUSE attached as the same-house reference; the stairs plate is the same flight seen from the top (mirrored, as the half-my-age lesson asked). **Read off the plates (§7, for the anchors — not a verdict):** in L-CARPARK the white van stands with its front to the camera at the back of the row, not two bays along with its back doors to the hatchback as the prompt asked — SC01's van will be placed by the shot prompt. Confirm or Fix each on the board.

**Set checks:** S1 tiers above · S2 daylight except SC06 (night, pendant in frame) · S3 profiles follow the orientation (east front, west back) · S4 consecutive scenes change place except SC01 → SC02 (one continuous moment: the car park, then into the car — a declared CONTINUOUS join). **The set closes here.**
